parameters.forbidden_hypergraph: K4^-: three triples on four vertices
parameters.constraint: every 4-vertex set spans at most 2 selected triples

search_metadata.budget_note: Fixed candidate count and seed by default. Explicit MATHBENCH_SEARCH_SECONDS enables a machine-dependent cutoff; runner limits still apply.

source_review.definition: 36-vertex three-uniform hypergraph, ordinary non-induced K4-minus forbidden: any four vertices span at most two triples. Maximize edge count. Complete four-edge hypergraphs also rejected.
source_review.primary_source: Falgas-Ravry, Pikhurko, Vaughan, Volec (JLMS2023 DOI10.1112/jlms.12722), section6.3 p27 explicitly lists ten H6 triples and permits iterated blow-ups. Ordinary density conjectured2/7 remains distinct from solved codegree and uniform-density tetrahedron problems. Source-level screening found no finite36 matching optimality proof.
source_review.reproduction: Root independently reconstructed the two-level balanced blow-up count10*6^3+6*10=2220. Human rebuilds published formula; no claim the paper tabulates2220 as a separate finite record.
source_review.independent_method: All36 vertex link graphs checked triangle-free. A forbidden K4-minus has a common vertex whose link is a triangle. Formal checker instead counts triples on each of58905 four-sets. Root direct double counting gives upper3570, not proof of actual optimum.
source_review.initial_and_search: Empty initial hypergraph valid with objective0; generic own greedy seed0 baseline1245 and evolution1246, no human/reference reads. Frozen human2220 positive permits ratio normalization even though initial objective0.
source_review.admission: Five strict budgeted programs and full broken-witness/claim-invariance/replay/cold-export/error/nonfinite/timeout controls passed.
